definitions.explanation: A fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from hardened mud — a mixture of clay and silt particles deposited in still water such as lakes or the deep sea. Often contains fossils and, in some regions, petroleum or natural gas.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地層|ちそう}→地層：06366_chisou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{泥岩|でいがん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦できている→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: This stratum is made of mudstone.

examples.english: Shell fossils were found in the mudstone.

examples.english: The slopes of this mountain have a lot of mudstone, so after rain one needs to watch out for landslides.

notes:
Composed of {泥|でい} (mud) and {岩|がん} (rock). The reading uses the on'yomi でい, typical of technical rock names. Formed when mud — very fine clay and silt — is compacted and cemented over long periods into a solid rock.

USAGE:
Appears in geology and earth-science contexts: textbooks, geological survey reports, news about landslides, and discussions of oil and gas reservoirs (many source rocks for petroleum are mudstones). Japanese hillsides with mudstone layers are known for being slide-prone, so the word also appears in disaster-prevention reporting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {泥岩|でいがん}⟦{層|そう}→層：12441_sou⟧: mudstone layer / stratum
- {泥岩|でいがん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to consist of mudstone
- ⟦{化石|かせき}→化石：11796_kaseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{含|ふく}む→含む：01982_fukumu⟧{泥岩|でいがん}: fossil-bearing mudstone
- {黒色|こくしょく}{泥岩|でいがん}: black mudstone (often rich in organic matter)
- {泥岩|でいがん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{風化|ふうか}→風化：17583_fuuka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: mudstone weathers / erodes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{砂岩|さがん}→砂岩：25999_sagan⟧: sandstone — made of sand-sized grains; coarser than {泥岩|でいがん}
- {礫岩|れきがん}: conglomerate — made of rounded pebbles cemented together
- {頁岩|けつがん}: shale — a fissile (easily splitting) variety of mudstone; often grouped with {泥岩|でいがん}
- {粘板岩|ねんばんがん}: slate — a low-grade metamorphic rock formed from shale or mudstone
- ⟦{堆積岩|たいせきがん}→堆積岩：23353_taisekigan⟧: sedimentary rock — the broader category that {泥岩|でいがん} belongs to
